entries.title: Tournament and editing
entries.name: 01-tournament-and-editing
entries.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Make one complete polished landscape 16:9 illustrated presentation board for HypeReel. The attached screenshot is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not content to copy. Match its neat Excalidraw whiteboard aesthetic: warm white background edge to edge (no black border), fine hand-drawn charcoal outlines, readable handwritten labels, softly rounded containers, careful grid alignment, purple headings, restrained pastel orange, green, lavender and blue accents. Crisp generous whitespace. Detailed charming little illustrated people, basketball scenes, filmstrips, arrows, UI vignettes and meaningful icons carry the story. Professional, visually engaging and organized, not messy. Use only short labels and a few key numbers; NO transcript paragraphs, no wall of text, no decorative illegible scribbles. Each board must tell its story visually at a glance. Large readable lettering. No photo-realism or 3D.
Board 1 of 5. Title "HypeReel" subtitle "A weekend of basketball. Hours of editing." Main story arranged in three connected illustrated scenes: left a wide isometric tournament hall with many miniature basketball courts, colorful teams, coaches and parents filming from sidelines, labelled "Tournament weekend"; center an overwhelmed parent at a laptop with a very long tangled filmstrip, huge clock, many marked cuts, label "Manual editing", chips "60-minute recording" and "3–4 hours per reel"; right the same parent happily reviewing a concise basketball highlight reel on screen with 6 tiny colored clips and a play button, label "Reviewed highlights". Above tournament show neat three statistic chips "421 teams", "36 courts", "3 days". Bottom a simple small calendar and US-map vignette with many tournament pins labelled "All season". A small orange estimate badge "≈7,000 editing hours / weekend" with tiny qualifier "Illustrative estimate". Final green outlined banner "HypeReel prototype • Live 10-minute demo". Preserve illustrated depth and storytelling without dense prose. Do not imply the prototype eliminates every editing hour.

entries.prompt:

Each board must tell its story visually at a glance. Large readable lettering. No photo-realism or 3D.
Board 2 of 5. Title "Inside HypeReel" subtitle "A recipe-driven LangGraph workflow". This is an accurate architecture diagram with illustrated icons. Top-left policy card "YAML recipe" with exactly three small settings "Events", "Duration budget", "Exclusions"; feeds "Plan". Main upper row sequential nodes and clear arrows left-to-right: "Plan" (route map) -> "Ingest" (video file) -> "Propose" (waveform + moving basketball player, label "Audio + motion") -> "Scoreboard" (grey dashed optional box, label "Inactive in demo") -> "Gemini" (basketball filmstrip, label "Video segments") -> "Select" (scissors + measured timeline, label "Duration budget"). A clear downward arrow at right feeds a lower row flowing RIGHT TO LEFT: "Metadata judge" (clipboard, short label "Text only") -> "Review clips" (human watching small video, orange gate number 1) -> "Render + summary" (clapperboard and six connected clips) -> "Approve delivery" (human watching completed reel, orange gate number 2) -> "Download" (local file icon). From Metadata judge a purple return arrow back to Select with exact label "At most 1 re-selection". Clearly point this arrow only to Select. Orange human gates visibly emphasized. Footer three tiny illustrated output cards "Previews", "Reel", "Logs". Short caveat labels "Other domains need validation" and "External upload not implemented". No cloud upload destination, no claim judge watches video. Balanced readable two-row composition.
entries.correction: Edit the attached illustration with surgical corrections. Preserve all illustrations, color, typography, layout and all unrelated content. Add a clear purple forward arrow DOWN from the bottom-left part of the '7. Select' box, bending left into the TOP of '8. Metadata judge'. This is the essential Select -> judge forward connection. Keep the existing right-side upward 'At most 1 re-selection' arrow as a separate RETURN from judge to Select. In the YAML recipe card replace '3–5 min' with 'Configurable'; replace 'Team games' with 'Event types'. All labels must fit neatly. No other changes.

Board 3 of 5. Title "The live demo" subtitle "From recording to a human-reviewed reel". Make a beautiful storyboard of three large browser mockup panels with hand-drawn illustrations, numbered 1, 2, 3. Panel 1 "Configure + analyze": form fields "East Bay excerpt", "Both teams", "10-minute source", a "Find highlights" button, beneath tiny real stage indicators "Plan → Analyze → Select → Judge". Flow arrows clearly connect the panels. Across bottom three spacious metric chips with meaningful icons: "6 distinct clips", "87-second reel", "7m 49s processing". Small caption "Verified run • Model suggestions for human review". Show this as an illustrative storyboard, not an exact screenshot or audited accuracy guarantee. Include a person reviewing screen and a jersey-23 basketball player as charming motifs. No long prose.

Board 4 of 5. Title "What the evaluations show" subtitle "Small development-window comparison". Left illustration: two open game folders containing basketball filmstrips with a short label "2 development games"; next to them a third lavender folder with a prominent padlock, label "Final test • sealed". Center/right dominant hand-drawn horizontal bar chart, accurate common zero baseline and linear lengths with axis 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%. Exact three rows: "MiniCPM" 12.5%, "Gemini video" 37.0%, "Gemini + transcript" 34.8%. Gemini video green, transcript lavender, MiniCPM grey-blue. Metric label "micro-F1". Show the green bar slightly longer than lavender and about 3 times grey-blue. Below chart three illustrated stat chips "8 windows", "14 reference events", "12 categories". Bottom an orange outlined sign with flag icon "Release criteria unmet", and short label "Not full-game accuracy". A slim footer shows a timeline with a magnifying glass and gaps being inspected, caption "Next: temporal evidence + candidate coverage". No upward success arrow that falsely suggests transcript improved scores. Avoid unsupported accuracy claims or fabricated extra statistics. Beautiful clear chart and engaging drawings.
entries.correction: Edit only the chart heading on this illustrated board. The heading currently incorrectly says '2. Model performance on held-out test (micro-F1)'. Replace that ENTIRE heading with the exact words '2. Development-window results (micro-F1)'. These results are from DEVELOPMENT windows, NOT the sealed final test. Do not write 'held-out test' anywhere. Preserve every other element unchanged: all three bars, the 12.5%, 37.0%, 34.8% values, axis, illustrations, sealed folder, colors, layout and footer. Keep impeccable handwritten typography.
